A cylinder 101.6 mm (4 in) in diameter was pushed into a bed of dense red scoria ([RS]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"}), and the load on it was recorded against its penetration. This is a load-penetration test ([LPT]{.term title="load-penetration test: a tool is pushed into a soil bed and the load is recorded against depth" tabindex="0"}), run at 0.423 mm/s in a bed of bulk density 825 kg/m³.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Data available:** 26 points read from the printed figure. One of them is still under review. Student reviewers have checked 7 of them on the scan, and two reviewers confirmed 6.
:::

Codes on this card: RS, red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded; Gp, peak deceleration of the dynamic penetrometer, in g; D50, grain size that half of the soil, by weight, is finer than; D95, grain size that 95 percent of the soil, by weight, is finer than; Cu, uniformity coefficient.

A simulation of this test is compared with the measurement through the axial force the soil exerts on the cylinder, the force the load cell measured, against the cylinder's penetration below the original soil surface. A comparison states where it puts the zero of force and of penetration, and whether the cylinder's own weight is included. The [Simulate a test](../simulate/index.qmd) page walks through the steps.

## Measured data

![Load against penetration: this test in red, the other tests printed in Fig. 2-42 in gray. The error bars on the red curve are its reading bounds. The round markers are the curve's marked features (start, peaks, troughs, end); filled ones were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not. The two hollow markers near 39 mm are competing readings of the same trough, still being settled; they are one feature, not two. Click to enlarge.](../img/plots/b68-lpt-024.png){.lightbox}

[Download the points (CSV)](../files/data/experiments/b68-lpt-024/observations.csv){.btn .btn-primary .me-2 .mb-2} [Download the reading record (JSON)](../files/data/experiments/b68-lpt-024/series.json){.btn .btn-outline-primary .me-2 .mb-2}

The CSV file gives penetration in m (`x_si`) and load in N (`y_si`), each with its reading bound (`x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`), and the status of each point. The JSON file gives the units, the conversion factors and how the points were read. A reading bound says how precisely a point could be read from the printed figure, typically 0.55 mm in penetration and 21 N in load here. It is not the scatter of the experiment, which the report does not give. [Both readings drawn over the scanned figure](../figures/index.qmd#check-f2-42).
